LESSON: ORAL EXPRESSION, ACTIVE LISTENING

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: GERMAN
Strand: Listening and Speaking
Topic 1.1: Oral Expression, Active listening

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Oral Expression, Active listening. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: how one is doing (z.B. Wie heißen Sie?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. recognize structures and expressions for oral interaction
2. appreciate the role of structures and expressions in communication

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: ORAL EXPRESSION, ACTIVE LISTENING
Subject: GERMAN · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Oral Expression, Active listening helps you succeed in GERMAN. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: ORAL EXPRESSION, ACTIVE LISTENING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Recognize structures and expressions for oral interaction

What this means
In this part you learn to recognize structures and expressions for oral interaction. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: recognize structures and expressions for oral interaction.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Oral Expression, Active listening”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can recognize structures and expressions for oral interaction. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Appreciate the role of structures and expressions in communication

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the role of structures and expressions in communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the role of structures and expressions in communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Oral Expression, Active listening to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the role of structures and expressions in communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Oral Expression, Active listening is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Oral Expression, Active listening”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: recognize structures and expressions for oral interaction)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Oral Expression, Active listening to a partner. (skill: appreciate the role of structures and expressions in communication)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Oral Expression, Active listening to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: recognize structures and expressions for oral interaction.
3. Practise this skill: appreciate the role of structures and expressions in communication.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Oral Expression, Active listening from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Oral Expression, Active listening: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Oral Expression, Active listening?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. how one is doing (z.B. Wie heißen Sie?
2. where they come from and/or stay (z.B. Woher How do we improve our vocabulary?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Oral Expression, Active listening means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: recognize structures and expressions for oral interaction.
5. Be able to: appreciate the role of structures and expressions in communication.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
